page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The show must go on
title: The show must go on
topic: Language for presenting a new product
description:
It's an exciting day for Tip Top Trading – the launch of its latest product, the plastic aubergine. The launch is taking place at a swanky hotel and lots of clients have turned up – but there's one important person missing. Will the team be able to present their new product effectively?
This episode focuses on the language that you might use when launching a new product at a presentation.
phrases: It is made of the highest quality plastic and I'm convinced it's something your business needs.
This product has been designed to the highest specifications. It's tough and durable.
It is the perfect decoration on any café or restaurant table.
We can offer you a generous discount. Plus, all our products come with a money back guarantee.

listening_challenge.question: In her presentation, what does Anna suggest using the plastic aubergine for?
listening_challenge.answer: As a perfect decoration on tables in cafés and restaurants.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome back to English at Work. It's an exciting day for Tip Top Trading. It's launching its latest product – the plastic aubergine. The launch is taking place at a swanky hotel; lots of clients have turned up - but there's one important person missing.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Has anyone seen Anna?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: I haven't seen her all morning. Tom, you were with her last.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: That was last night at the pub. She was drowning her sorrows.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Drowning her sorrows?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah. She saw Dave from IT with another woman – Julie from accounts, actually. She was very upset.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh poor Anna.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: So you left her drowning in the pub? And who's got the prototype aubergine to show at the launch?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh no! Anna has. It's in her bag. What are we going to do?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Panic!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: No Denise. Calm down. I'll just have to make a start and I'm sure Anna will turn up. OK, here goes. Excuse me everyone, could you all gather round? Our presentation is about to begin.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I'll change the slides for you on the computer Paul. I'm good with technology.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Okey dokey. Ermm…ladies and gentlemen, thank you for coming to our presentation. We have something very exciting to…ermm…show you and it's not a fruit…ha ha…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: …and here it is – fresh from the factory – our plastic aubergine!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna, you're just in time.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I know. I think I drank a bit too much last night and now I can't remember what to say.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well, you need to convince everyone that this is best product on the market and that it's something they really want. You could say "We believe this high quality product is something your business needs" – and, "Our new product has been designed to the highest specifications" – and tell people that "This product is the perfect decoration on any café or restaurant table" – tell them that, and the orders will come flying in!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What? They'll send them by aeroplane?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: No Anna! Just do your presentation and see what happens.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: OK then. Yes everyone, this aubergine may look good enough to eat but it is made of the highest quality plastic and I'm convinced it's something your business needs.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Err yes, that's right. It may be plastic but it is… fantastic!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thank you Paul. This product has been designed to the highest specifications. It's tough and durable.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Yeah but why would I want to buy it?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: 'Cos it's cheap mate!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No Tom. It's because it is the perfect decoration on any café or restaurant table. It shows you're serious about food.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: And it doesn't go mouldy.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes. We're taking orders today and… and…

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: And? And what, Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I don't know what to say next.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Offer them a discount and a guarantee.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh right. If you place an order for more than 1,000, we can offer you a generous discount. Plus, all our products come with a money-back guarantee.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: I like it!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well done Anna. She gave a clear presentation, and sounded enthusiastic about the product. Here's a reminder of some of the things she said:
It is made of the highest quality plastic and I'm convinced it’s something your business needs.
This product has been designed to the highest specifications. It's tough and durable.
It is the perfect decoration on any café or restaurant table.
We can offer you a generous discount. Plus, all our products come with a money-back guarantee.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks for listening. Tom has a few slides to show, which illustrate how the aubergine has been designed. Tom… Tom?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh no, it's frozen, the slides won't change.

transcript.speaker: Dave
transcript.text: It's OK, I can fix it, I am the IT guy after all.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Dave? What are you doing here? Cheating on Anna like that. Here Anna, give me that aubergine.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Tom, no!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: There, that's for upsetting Anna.

transcript.speaker: Dave
transcript.text: Ha ha - missed me!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Ha! Well the aubergine's certainly tough and durable.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Tom, Anna, I think we'd better talk about this back in my office.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Crikey! That was certainly a spectacular presentation. Let's hope Tom’s outburst doesn't stop the orders flying in – but not via the window! Find out next time on English at Work. Bye!
